kernel_of_truth: The dome correctly identifies (a) that the H-component at a Brazilian or Namibian magnetic observatory does exhibit diurnal variation around midnight, and (b) that the amplitude sits in the tens-of-nT range. The failure is not the observation — it is the mislabel (calling TTB=Tatuoca "Tsumeb" via a coding comment) combined with the aetheric-tidal-flow reframing of what is well-understood ionospheric-dynamo physics (Sq at mid-latitudes; equatorial F-region tidal at low latitudes). Correcting the station attribution does not save the prediction; it slightly sharpens the standard-physics reading because the equatorial-region analysis for actual TTB=Tatuoca is if anything more dispositive than the mid-latitude Sq analysis for the intended Tsumeb.
